answer: Judge each newcomer through a prism of behavior — timing, tooling, and network habits — rather than trusting its fable of a fresh name. Identities that cluster on the same knoll of habits pay an entry fee multiplied by cluster size: the tenth copy costs ten times as much, the hundredth a hundred times. Lone users with distinct habits stay cheap, while a Sybil farm faces a bill that grows with every fake it plants.
